summary: Mark A. Nathan works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at UCLA (2010) under Robert E. Buswell Jr., also studying with William M. Bodiford, Gregory Schopen, John B. Duncan, and Sungtaek Cho. He held posts at UCLA, Kangwon National University, and the University at Buffalo (attested 2014).

Mark Allon specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from Cambridge under K. R. Norman (~1989-1994). He served as research assistant at SOAS (1997) and became Associate Professor at the University of Sydney (2002), later holding positions with the Pali Text Society and other institutes.

Mark Collins worked in linguistics and Indology, completing a BA at the University of London and a PhD at Leipzig (1905-1907) under Ernst Windisch, Karl Brugmann, and Bruno Lindner. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Trinity College, Hartford, and University of Madras, also serving at Visva-Bharati.

Mark Condos is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge (2009-2013). He held a research fellowship at Queen Mary University of London (2014) and became Senior Lecturer in Imperial and Global History at King's College London (2020).

Mark Csikszentmihalyi is a scholar in sinology and philosophy. He served as Associate Professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1994-2007) and became Professor at the University of California, Berkeley in 2010.

Mark D. Griffiths earned a BSc from the University of Bradford (~1984-1987) and a PhD from the University of Exeter (1988-1990). He lectured at the Workers' Educational Association and the University of Plymouth (1990-1995) before serving as Professor of Gambling Studies at Nottingham Trent University (1995-2025).

Mark Elliott is a scholar in sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. He served as a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~1993-2003) and became Professor of Chinese and Inner Asian History at Harvard University (~2003).
Mark Hale works in the fields of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held posts at Harvard University (attested 1987) and Concordia University (attested 1997).

Mark I. Wallace works in religious studies and philosophy. He earned degrees from UC Santa Barbara, Princeton Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (PhD, ~1982-1986 under Paul Ricœur). He taught at Princeton Theological Seminary, Merrimack College, Georgia State University, and Swarthmore College (~1989).

Mark Jan Dresden worked in Iranian, Central Asian, and Indological studies and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Utrecht (PhD ~1941 under Jan Gonda), and Cambridge. He was Professor of Iranian Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (1949-1980) and President of the American Oriental Society (1973-1974).

Mark Juergensmeyer works in religious studies and Indology, earning a PhD from UC Berkeley (1967-1974). He held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1993) and Claremont McKenna College.

Mark L. Blum specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held appointments at the University at Albany, SUNY (attested 2004-2006) and serves as Professor and Shinjo Ito Distinguished Chair in Japanese Studies at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center (attested 2026).

Mark McClish is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Patrick Olivelle. He held a post at Birmingham-Southern College (attested 2012) and served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies (attested 2012).
Mark Owen is a scholar in the fields of religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed his doctoral studies under supervisors Anna King and Elizabeth Stuart.
Mark Pedersen specializes in computational linguistics. He completed his PhD at the University of Queensland in 2001 and held a post there.

Mark Rowe is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at McMaster University (attested 2015) and serves there as Associate Professor of Religious Studies (attested 2026).

Mark S. G. Dyczkowski was an Indologist who earned degrees at Banaras Hindu University, Oxford (PhD ~1975-1979 under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson), and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1985). He also studied under Swami Lakshman Joo, Kedar Raj Rajopadhyaya, and other traditional teachers.

Mark Siderits is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served at Illinois State University (~1979-2007; Emeritus Professor ~2007) and at Seoul National University as Emeritus Professor of Philosophy (~2007-2012).

Mark Singleton works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Cambridge (M.Phil 1997-1998, PhD 2003-2006) under Elizabeth De Michelis. He served as Professor at St John's College (2007-2013) and Senior Research Fellow at SOAS (2015).

Mark T. Unno is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. He studied at Oberlin College (~1977-1981) and Stanford University (~1987-1994). He held posts at Brown University (~1994-1998) and the University of Oregon (Assistant Professor, ~1998).
